mainTopic: Mourning and the רגל: how the festival cancels שבעה and שלשים, אבא שאול's מקצת היום ככולו, the source for שלשים, and whether festival days count toward שלשים
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא: a רגל cancels שבעה if the mourner kept three days before it, and cancels שלשים if he kept eight. The תנא קמא says he must shave on ערב הרגל or wait until after שלשים. אבא שאול lets him shave after the festival, because he holds מקצת היום ככולו, so the seventh day counts twice. רב's rule that a mourner may bathe once the comforters leave follows אבא שאול. אביי, רבא and the נהרדעי disagree on how far we follow אבא שאול on the seventh and thirtieth days. The נהרדעי rely on שמואל's rule that in mourning we follow the lenient view. The גמרא learns the thirty days from a נזיר through the word פרע, and learns the נזיר's thirty days from the גימטריא of יהיה. Everyone agrees that if the third day falls on ערב הרגל, the mourner may not bathe until evening. Finally, אביי asks רבא whether festival days count toward שלשים, רבא says they do not, and אביי begins challenging him from a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא on how a festival cancels mourning periods
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. A burial three days before a רגל cancels שבעה, and a burial eight days before cancels שלשים. The mourner shaves on ערב הרגל, and if he did not, he may not shave after the festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: One who buries his dead relative three days before a festival, the decree of seven days is cancelled for him. If he buried eight days before a festival, the decree of thirty days is cancelled for him, and he shaves on the eve of the festival. If he did not shave on the eve of the festival, he is forbidden to shave after the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the words 'but isn't it taught' to test what was said just before. The ברייתא lays out when a רגל cancels שבעה and when it cancels שלשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three days of mourning before the festival are enough for the festival to wipe out the rest of שבעה. Eight days are enough for it to wipe out שלשים. This first opinion adds a catch: the mourner gets one window to shave, on ערב הרגל. If he misses it, the ban on shaving returns after the festival until thirty days are complete.

keyTerms.meaning: The rules of the first seven days of mourning
The rules of the thirty-day mourning period, such as no haircuts

steps.confusionAlert: The festival does not just 'pause' mourning here. It cancels the period completely. That is why the question is only about shaving, which is the one thing the mourner still needs a chance to do.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: one who buries his dead relative
three days before the festival,
the decree of seven is cancelled for him;
eight days before the festival,
the decree of thirty is cancelled for him,
and he shaves on the eve of the festival.
phrases.notes: Literally 'shaves,' but it covers cutting hair too, which is the main thing banned during שלשים.

phrases.english: If he did not shave on the eve of the festival,
he is forbidden to shave after the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the statement made just before, on the earlier part of the daf, using a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The previous statement about shaving after the festival
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first opinion in the ברייתא says a mourner who missed shaving on ערב הרגל may not shave afterward.

steps.title: אבא שאול permits shaving after the festival
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול says the mourner may shave after the festival. Just as three days of mourning cancel שבעה, seven days of mourning cancel שלשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: He is permitted to shave after the festival. Just as the מצוה of three days cancels the decree of seven, so the מצוה of seven days cancels the decree of thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with אבא שאול, who disagrees with the first opinion and allows shaving after the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול reasons from a comparison. The festival fully wipes out שבעה once three days were kept, with no catch attached. In the same way, once seven days were kept, שלשים is fully wiped out, so the ban on shaving never comes back.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
He is permitted to shave after the festival,
for just as the מצוה of three days
cancels the decree of seven,
so too the מצוה of seven days
cancels the decree of thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mourner whose שלשים was cancelled by the festival may shave after the festival, even if he did not shave on ערב הרגל.

steps.title: Why does אבא שאול say seven instead of eight?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אבא שאול speaks of seven days when the rule we learned requires eight days to cancel שלשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Seven? But we learned eight!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that אבא שאול's wording does not match the rule. That rule says eight days before the festival are needed to cancel שלשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says eight days, yet אבא שאול speaks of 'the מצוה of seven.' The גמרא wants to know how seven days can cancel שלשים when the stated number is eight.

phrases.english: Seven? But we learned eight!
phrases.notes: This points back to the rule of 'eight days before the festival' cancelling the thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of אבא שאול's reasoning
steps.kashyaTarget: אבא שאול's phrase 'the מצוה of seven'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule we learned needs eight days, not seven, to cancel שלשים.

steps.title: Part of a day counts as a whole day
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול holds מקצת היום ככולו, so the seventh day counts both as the last day of שבעה and as a day of שלשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול holds that part of a day counts like the whole day, and so the seventh day counts for him toward both this and that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Seven and eight are really the same count, because the seventh day counts twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under מקצת היום ככולו, once the morning of day seven passes, שבעה is over. The rest of that day already counts toward שלשים. So the seven days of mourning already include the start of שלשים, which matches the 'eight days' in the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of a day counts as the whole day

steps.whyThisMatters: מקצת היום ככולו is a basic principle in the laws of mourning. It explains why שבעה ends on the morning of the seventh day.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul holds:
part of the day is like all of it,

phrases.aramaic: וְיוֹם שְׁבִיעִי עוֹלֶה לוֹ לְכָאן וּלְכָאן.
phrases.english: and the seventh day counts for him toward both this and that.
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means the seven days of mourning and the thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about seven versus eight
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the underlying principle (מקצת היום ככולו) so the numbers fit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought seven days falls short of the eight that are required.
steps.terutzMaskana: The seventh day counts as both the end of שבעה and part of שלשים, so the seven days match the eight.

steps.title: The halacha follows אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, in the name of רבינא בר שילא, rules like אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of רבינא בר שילא: The הלכה is like אבא שאול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling in the argument from the ברייתא. The halacha follows אבא שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, a mourner whose שלשים was cancelled by the festival may shave after the festival, even if he did not shave on ערב הרגל.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows אבא שאול. A festival that cancels שלשים cancels it fully, so the mourner may shave even after the festival.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רָבִינָא בַּר שֵׁילָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Ravina bar Sheila said:
The halacha is like Abba Shaul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument between the first opinion and אבא שאול
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is like אבא שאול: shaving is permitted after the festival.

steps.title: The חכמים agree when the eighth day is a שבת on ערב הרגל
steps.stepSummary: Even the חכמים agree with אבא שאול when the eighth day of mourning falls on a שבת that is also ערב הרגל. In that case the mourner may shave on Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים agree with אבא שאול that when his eighth day falls on שבת which is ערב הרגל, he may shave on ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a case where the חכמים agree with אבא שאול. Here the mourner may shave on day seven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the חכמים want him to shave on the eighth day, which is ערב הרגל. If that day is שבת, shaving is forbidden then. So the חכמים let him shave on Friday, the seventh day, which is exactly what אבא שאול's counting allows.

phrases.english: And the Sages agree with Abba Shaul
when his eighth day falls
to be on Shabbat that is the eve of the festival,
that he is permitted to shave on Friday.
phrases.notes: Friday here is his seventh day, which is why this counts as agreeing with אבא שאול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case where the opposing side agrees with אבא שאול
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the eighth day is a שבת that is ערב הרגל, the mourner may shave on Friday, his seventh day.

steps.title: Whose view does רב's bathing rule follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is behind רב's ruling that a mourner may bathe as soon as the comforters get up to leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion matches what רב עמרם said in the name of רב: a mourner, once the comforters stand up to leave him, is allowed to bathe?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical ruling from רב and asks which opinion it is based on. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bathing is forbidden during שבעה. If the mourner may bathe on the seventh day as soon as the comforters leave, then only part of the seventh day was kept as mourning. That only works if part of a day counts as a whole day.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is this
that Rav Amram said that Rav said:
A mourner, once they have stood up,
the comforters, to leave him,
he is permitted to bathe?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב עַמְרָם אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects a practical ruling of רב to the dispute about מקצת היום ככולו discussed earlier.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view does רב's bathing rule follow?

steps.title: It follows אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: רב's ruling matches אבא שאול, who holds that part of a day counts as a whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is it? אבא שאול's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: רב's ruling follows אבא שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only אבא שאול counts a short part of the seventh day as a full day of mourning. That is why the mourner can bathe once the comforters leave.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the view of אבא שאול

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with Abba Shaul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב's ruling follows אבא שאול's principle of מקצת היום ככולו.

steps.title: אביי: the הלכה follows אבא שאול on day seven
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules like אבא שאול on the seventh day. He adds that on the thirtieth day even the חכמים agree that part of the day counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the הלכה follows אבא שאול on the seventh day. On the thirtieth day the חכמים agree with אבא שאול, because there we say that part of the day is like the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his practical ruling on how far we follow אבא שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי adds something new. On the thirtieth day there is no dispute at all, and everyone agrees part of the day counts. So the argument is only about the seventh day, and there אביי follows אבא שאול.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of the day counts as the whole day

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The halakha follows Abba Shaul on the seventh day,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְאַבָּא שָׁאוּל בְּיוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים,
phrases.english: and the Rabbis agree with Abba Shaul on the thirtieth day,
for we say that part of the day is like the whole of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הֲלָכָה כְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל בְּיוֹם שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from identifying the source of רב's rule to a practical ruling on the seventh and thirtieth days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Follow אבא שאול on day seven; on day thirty everyone agrees part of the day counts.

steps.title: רבא: follow אבא שאול only on day thirty
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי. He follows אבא שאול on the thirtieth day but not on the seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the הלכה follows אבא שאול on the thirtieth day, but it does not follow אבא שאול on the seventh day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different ruling from אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the seventh day is stricter. The mourner must keep the whole seventh day, so he may not bathe in the morning. On the thirtieth day, though, part of the day is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: But the הלכה is not so

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up אביי and רבא. אביי follows אבא שאול on day seven (and on day thirty everyone agrees). רבא follows him only on day thirty.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל בְּיוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים,
phrases.english: Rava said: The halakha follows Abba Shaul on the thirtieth day,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל בְּיוֹם שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.english: but the halakha does not follow Abba Shaul on the seventh day.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל בְּיוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling that disagrees with אביי about the seventh day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Part of the day counts on day thirty but not on day seven.

steps.title: נהרדעי: follow אבא שאול on both days
steps.stepSummary: The נהרדעי rule like אבא שאול on both the seventh and the thirtieth day, based on שמואל's rule that in mourning we follow the lenient view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The נהרדעי say: the הלכה follows אבא שאול in both cases. For שמואל said: in mourning, the הלכה follows the one who is lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion is given, along with its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נהרדעי use a general rule from שמואל. In the laws of mourning, we follow the more lenient opinion. Since אבא שאול is the lenient one on both days, we follow him on both.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of the city נהרדעא
In this case and in that case (both days)
In mourning, the הלכה follows the lenient view

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views: אביי follows אבא שאול on day seven. רבא follows him only on day thirty. The נהרדעי follow him on both days, because in mourning we follow the lenient view.
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's rule (הלכה כדברי המיקל באבל) is a general rule. It is used again and again in the laws of mourning.

phrases.english: And the Sages of Neharde'a say:
The halakha follows Abba Shaul in both this and that,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הַמֵּיקֵל בְּאֵבֶל.
phrases.english: for Shmuel said: The halakha follows the words of the lenient one in mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּנְהַרְדָּעֵי אָמְרִי: הֲלָכָה כְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל בָּזוֹ וּבָזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, most lenient position after אביי and רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Follow אבא שאול on both day seven and day thirty, because in mourning we follow the lenient view.

steps.title: Where do the thirty days come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the thirty-day mourning period.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know the thirty days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes topic and asks for the source of שלשים. This sets up the derivation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole discussion so far took for granted that there is a thirty-day period with a ban on haircuts. Now the גמרא wants to know where in the תורה that number comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

phrases.english: Thirty days, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rulings about day thirty to the source of the thirty days itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the thirty days of mourning.

steps.title: Learned from נזיר through the word פרע
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שוה links the word פרע said to mourners with the same word said about a נזיר. Just as a נזיר grows his hair thirty days, so does a mourner.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it from the word פרע, which appears here and also with a נזיר. Here it says: Do not let your heads grow loose. There it says: He shall let the hair of his head grow long. Just as there it is thirty days, so too here it is thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a גזירה שוה, matching the same word in two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אהרן and his remaining sons were told not to let their hair grow, even though mourners normally do. This shows that a regular mourner does let his hair grow. Since the same word פרע is used for a נזיר, who grows his hair thirty days, the mourner's ban on haircuts also lasts thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזיר, who may not cut his hair
Just as there, so too here (the גזירה שוה formula)

steps.whatToRemember: The thirty days of שלשים come from a גזירה שוה of פרע and פרע with a נזיר.

phrases.english: It is learned from "pera" and "pera" with a nazirite.
It is written here: "Let your heads not grow loose,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:6, said to אהרן and his sons. It shows that a regular mourner does let his hair grow.

phrases.english: and it is written there: "He shall let the hair of his head grow long,"

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן שְׁלֹשִׁים, אַף כָּאן שְׁלֹשִׁים.
phrases.english: just as there it is thirty, so too here it is thirty.
phrases.notes: This assumes a נזיר grows his hair thirty days. The next step asks how we know that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of the word פרע links mourning to נזיר, whose hair-growing period is thirty days.

steps.title: Where do we know a נזיר's thirty days from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that a נזיר grows his hair for thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, regarding a נזיר, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The previous step learned the mourner's thirty days from a נזיר. Now the גמרא asks how we know that a נזיר himself has thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה only works if the number thirty is clear in the source case. The תורה never says outright that a נזיר grows his hair for thirty days, so the גמרא needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning the case of the נזיר
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And there, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: "There" means the נזיר from the last step. The question is where his thirty days come from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the number thirty in the case the גזירה שוה relied on
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a נזיר's hair-growing period is thirty days

steps.title: An unspecified נזירות lasts thirty days, from the גימטריא of יהיה
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה says that a plain נזירות with no time given lasts thirty days, because the word יהיה adds up to thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: A plain נזירות lasts thirty days. What is the reason? The פסוק says "he shall be holy," and the word יהיה adds up to thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה answers the question. A נזיר who did not say how long his vow lasts keeps it for thirty days, and he learns this from the letters of the word יהיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters of יהיה are י=10, ה=5, י=10, ה=5, which add up to thirty. This gives the number thirty for a נזיר, and the גזירה שוה from the last step carries it over to a mourner.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזירות vow taken without saying how long it lasts
The number value of the letters of a word

steps.whatToRemember: A mourner's thirty days come from the נזיר through the word פרע. The נזיר's thirty days come from the number value of יהיה, which is thirty.

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
A plain naziriteship lasts thirty days.
What is the reason?
The verse says: "He shall be holy."
The letters of yihye add up to thirty.
phrases.notes: י is 10 and ה is 5, so י-ה-י-ה makes 10+5+10+5 = 30.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה: סְתַם נְזִירוּת שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by giving the source for a נזיר's thirty days
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A plain נזירות lasts thirty days, learned from the גימטריא of יהיה in the פסוק "קדוש יהיה"

steps.title: When the third day falls on ערב הרגל, the mourner may not bathe until evening
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says that everyone agrees: if the mourner's third day falls on ערב הרגל, he may not bathe until evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: Everyone agrees that when his third day falls on ערב הרגל, he is forbidden to bathe until evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule about a mourner whose third day of mourning falls on the day before a רגל. Everyone agrees he may not bathe until that evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Everyone" includes אבא שאול, who usually says part of a day counts as a whole day. Here even he agrees that the morning of the third day does not end the bathing ban. The mourner must wait until evening.

keyTerms.meaning: The day before a יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this goes against אבא שאול. The word הכל means that even אבא שאול agrees in this case.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
Everyone agrees
that when his third day falls
on the eve of the Festival,
he is forbidden to bathe until the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: הַכֹּל מוֹדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of counting part of a day and gives a case where everyone agrees
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the third day of mourning falls on ערב הרגל, bathing is forbidden until evening, even according to אבא שאול

steps.title: רב פפי and רב פפא rule like רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמיה בריה דרב יהושע reports that רב פפי and רב פפא ruled the הלכה like רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמיה בריה דרב יהושע said: I found רב פפי and רב פפא sitting and saying: The הלכה follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone reports hearing two אמוראים rule that the הלכה follows רב הונא's statement from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רב הונא's rule is one opinion, and רב פפי and רב פפא decide the הלכה like him. That makes his rule the final practice.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Neḥemya, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
I found Rav Pappi and Rav Pappa
sitting and saying:

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: The halakha follows Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: אַשְׁכַּחְתִּינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms רב הונא's rule as the practical הלכה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע

steps.title: Another version: all three said the rule together
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב נחמיה בריה דרב יוסף reports that רב פפי, רב פפא and רב הונא said the rule together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב נחמיה בריה דרב יוסף said: I found רב פפי, רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע sitting and saying: Everyone agrees that if his third day falls on ערב הרגל, he is forbidden to bathe until evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same report. It has a different reporter, and the rule is said by three אמוראים together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב הונא said the rule alone, and the others ruled like him. In this version, all three said the rule together. Either way, the practical rule is the same: no bathing until evening.
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, a mourner whose third day falls on ערב הרגל may not bathe until evening.

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Neḥemya, son of Rav Yosef, said:
I found Rav Pappi and Rav Pappa
and Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua,
sitting and saying:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים שֶׁאִם חָל שְׁלִישִׁי שֶׁלּוֹ
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that if his third day falls
on the eve of the Festival,
he is forbidden to bathe until the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of how the rule was passed down
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All three אמוראים together said that bathing is forbidden until evening when the third day falls on ערב הרגל

steps.title: אביי asks whether a רגל counts toward the thirty days
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבא: if someone buried his relative during a רגל, do the days of the רגל count toward the thirty days of mourning? He explains that he is not asking about the seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רבא: If he buried him on the רגל, does the רגל count toward the thirty days or not? I am not asking about the seven days, since the seven-day mourning does not apply on a רגל. I am asking about the thirty days, since the thirty-day mourning does apply on a רגל. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new question. If the burial happened during a רגל, do those festival days count toward the thirty days of mourning?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי makes the question narrow. The seven days clearly do not count, because שבעה is not kept at all on a רגל. But the thirty-day mourning is partly kept on a רגל, so maybe those days do count.

keyTerms.meaning: I am not asking about this

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not unsure about the seven days. He says outright that they do not count. His only question is about the thirty days.

phrases.english: Abaye asked Rava:
If he buried him on the Festival,
does the Festival count for him toward the thirty days,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין רֶגֶל עוֹלֶה לוֹ לְמִנְיַן שְׁלֹשִׁים?
phrases.english: or does the Festival not count for him toward the thirty days?
I am not asking about the count of seven,
because the seven-day mourning is not kept on the Festival.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי לְמִנְיַן שְׁלֹשִׁים,
phrases.english: What I am asking about is the count of thirty,
since the thirty-day mourning is kept on the Festival.
What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about counting the thirty days when the burial happened on a רגל
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether festival days count toward the thirty days of mourning when the burial happened on the רגל

steps.title: רבא answers: the Festival does not count toward the thirty
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers אביי that if someone buried his relative during a רגל, the days of the רגל do not count toward the thirty days of mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: The רגל does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a short, direct answer to the question אביי asked in the last step. The days of the רגל are not counted as part of the thirty days of mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי asked only about the thirty days, not the seven. רבא's answer is that the רגל is not counted for the thirty either. So the mourner starts counting his thirty days only after the רגל ends.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not count (literally, 'it does not go up' into the total)

phrases.english: He said to him: It does not count.
phrases.notes: רבא is answering אביי. 'It' means the days of the רגל, counted toward the thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers אביי's question from step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The days of the רגל do not count toward the thirty days for someone who buried during the רגל.

steps.title: אביי objects from a ברייתא about burial two days before a Festival
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא by quoting a ברייתא. Someone who buried his relative two days before a רגל counts five more days after the רגל. During those days others do his work, his servants work quietly inside his house, and the public does not need to come comfort him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected to רבא: If someone buries his dead relative two days before a רגל, he counts five days after the רגל. During those days his work is done by others, his servants and maidservants work privately inside his house, and the public does not need to busy themselves with him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins quoting a ברייתא to challenge רבא's answer. This is the opening of the ברייתא, and it continues past this point. The exact point of the challenge will become clear as the quote goes on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's case: the mourner already sat two days of שבעה before the רגל. After the רגל he finishes with five more days, which makes seven. It also lists the lighter rules for those five days: his work may be done for him by others, and the public need not come comfort him. אביי is building toward a point in this ברייתא that he believes goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Busy themselves with him, here meaning coming to comfort him

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at the end of this line and think you have the whole challenge. This is only the start of the ברייתא. The part that actually goes against רבא comes as the quote continues.

phrases.english: He objected to him: One who buries his dead relative
phrases.notes: אביי is now challenging רבא's answer from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: two days before the Festival —
counts five days after the Festival,
and his work is done by others,
and his menservants and maidservants work
privately inside his house,
and the public does not busy themselves with him,
phrases.notes: He means people don't need to come comfort him during these five days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 20 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the days of the רגל do not count toward the thirty days of mourning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי quotes a ברייתא about mourning around a רגל. Its continuation, on the next amud, is meant to show a different rule for how the רגל is counted.
